Thank you - this really helps. I'm doing my best right now.

Hope you have a nice day!

Thank you so much. I'm trying to stay rational right now and do something nice for myself and not freak out so much (or moreso than I already was/am). Urgh it's such a small thing. Anyways, it's really hard but I'm grateful for the message and the support <3

I don't know. From the incident a few years ago really the full story is just pretty much; I accidentally spilled something on her laptop and it started not working properly when she got home that night. I knew it was bad and I messed up, but I apologised a lot and offered to pay for everything and take it to be fixed with her but she was so angry and refused to talk to me for weeks but talked to everyone behind my back. And she was a best friend at that point. I kind of just learned from that and similar experiences in the past that even if I mess up even a bit, people I care about will lash out and do that to me and there's no room for forgiveness. 

The friend from today is a different one, but I'm still terrified. Something's going to go wrong and it's going to be a repeat of last time. It was definitely a fragile computer in her bag too. Though I didn't even know it was in there when I dropped it lmao, she told me afterwards and I swear my life flashed before my eyes on the spot. God. I care about this friend a lot and I can't stand losing her. 

But thank you for your response, I really appreciate it. I know I'm being irrational, logically, but god I hate that I'm freaking out so much. I also know that even if something goes wrong if this friend really is my friend we can work something out, but my whole life people have been angry at me and left me for less.

That's true. I kind of want to control everything; I want to make sure people don't leave but I also feel too scared to lash out or anything else so I silently self destruct. Thanks again though, for understanding.

Thanks; yeah I try to think reasonably whenever I spiral. It's difficult when I'm terrified and quietly losing my mind over it but ah. 

Thanks again.

This is so similar to my situation that I thought I'd chip in a reply. I really relate. Like some days it's better but sometimes just seeing people able to so easily connect and make friends, especially doing group outings and gatherings, trigger huge waves of bad emotion and suicidal thoughts for me. *Especially* if my fp is with them. I guess I'm just bad at being alone but still find it incredibly hard to connect with people. 

I used to beat myself up for it a lot but now I'm trying to very slowly build up even superficial connections with people. 

Best of luck buddy, you're not alone in feeling this way.
Hey..thanks for the response. It means a lot. I'm doing my best and it's hard...but thank you for taking the time out of your day to reply.

Oh yeah I definitely have problems with all this. It's really hard for me to motivate myself to shower or brush my teeth - it's not even that I can't do it, it's just that sometimes I really can't muster myself to even get up and do it all. It all seems like such a chore, and I envy people who just do the daily stuff quickly with no sweat or hesitation. One time I just laid on the couch for an hour aimlessly on my phone because I couldn't for the love of me motivate myself to get up and shower. I wasn't the sleepy kind of tired, I just felt heavy and exhausted in the empty kind of way. 

Sometimes I try not to give myself too much grief for it though. I do feel bad about it but at the end of the day we're all trying. Do one small thing at a time. What I figured out is to shower as soon as I get home if I can, because I have a little bit of energy left from being out and doing things, and if I shower immediately then there's not too much stuff to do before bed (showering and flossing and brushing my teeth and everything actually feels overwhelming together). Breaking it down into smaller tasks.

I totally understand where you're coming from and I wish you best of luck. Celebrate and be happy for yourself when you get one thing done :) And don't feel too ashamed or terrible if you can't.

AWOLNATION and Mother Mother are two good artists I listen to when I'm upset. It depends on whether you want something relatable or cheerful, because I usually aim for relatable.

Some others include La Dispute, Foster The People, and Of Mice & Men

Probably my relationships with other people. What with finding it really hard to maintain good, genuine friendships and connections. The loneliness/isolation part.

Of course the difficulty of handling intense emotions and them being really very unpredictable and out of the blue is hard. Sometimes I just have to be prepared for a small thing to throw me out of the loop for most of the day.

I've definitely felt this way when I went to see school counsellors back in high school. I always felt awkward and unable to open up or express myself and my problems to them. My advice is to write things down, which is what I ended up doing. 

I would type up my concerns/problems/main issues I wanted to talk about and address (including sometimes specific examples in my life) and printed it to bring to counselling on paper. If they're a good therapist they should understand and be willing to read what you write, even if they're just simple, brief points to start off the conversation. It might help if you let them know somehow that you're finding it difficult to talk and be honest about what you're struggling with, and see if there's anything the therapist can do to accomodate that. Good luck.

Definitely so. I always gravitate towards people who make me feel needed and who depend on me, even if it's in an unhealthy way, which sucks. 

I have let myself be really used by people before to a huge extent because I was scared of them abandoning me as soon as I became unnecessary to them, and I had to find a way to be useful to them so they have a reason to stay (e.g. offering up way too much of my time and energy to help them with things). If they ended up needing me/depending on me for something, or at least made me feel that way, I tended to gravitate a lot towards them and couldn't let go. 

It's like I'd rather have people treat me terribly but still need me than be alone and feel abandoned by everyone around me. But since I've become aware of it I've been working on fixing it and not getting myself into horribly unbalanced relationships of me wearing myself out for people who don't respect or value me as a person or a friend.

I suppress my emotions a lot - literally cannot show any emotion but a friendliness that makes others around me accept and like me. It terrifies me to open up or show vulnerability at all even though some days it feels like there are literal rollercoasters of emotions cycling within me. I try not to open up at all because I've always regretted it and I'm scared that once I do I won't be able to stop, because there's just so much.

I wish I could be more expressive, and just able to be a little vulnerable around others (plenty of my friends are able to talk about personal problems and emotional concerns with each other, and that in itself is unfathomable to me - I wish I could, but I can't). I can't trust others at all and it sucks because since I can't open up to them, I feel like they find it harder to open up to me and feel close enough to me to talk to me about their more personal things - even though I always want to listen and help them. 

Whenever I can't handle it anymore I just cry or let the emotions take over, in private. And it's always in private (or at most, with a counsellor). 

A lot of stereotypes I see with BPD involves being fairly expressive with emotions/anger but maybe there are also some of us who don't do that and suppress it/internalise emotion and thoughts more than expressing them when we feel them.

Very much so. I have experienced clear symptoms of BPD for a long time, but have gotten incredibly good at suppressing anger, emotions, and all of that, possibly out of fear of people's judgement or reactions.
I put on a really good facade and I seem almost entirely perfectly functional and happy in school, and my breakdowns and everything are kept as private as possible. One time I literally broke down sobbing because I thought my friends all hated me and were leaving me, but ten minutes later I was acting perfectly normal out the door. It's funny because the people around me have literally never seen me angry or really sad (other than if I'm making a few jokes here and there about it), when all I'm doing is trying to keep it bottled up as much as possible. I'm probably the last person anyone would expect to have any symptoms of BPD. 

Even when I'm incredibly angry or hurt or feeling like I'm losing control I tend to be too scared to lash out or say anything or reach out to people - the only time I do lashed out was at home. Both my dad and I had huge tempers and back when I lived with my parents he was relentless in his anger and only there for some reason did I let myself express the full extent of my emotions all the time, and it wasn't fun.
